title: Progressive Deployment Health: Canary, A/B & Shadow Monitoring in Console
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Add a consolidated Console view that surfaces health and divergence signals for progressive deployments (canary, A/B tests, shadowing) and ties high-level metrics to traces and per-route token-level cost. The feature should make it straightforward for engineers and PMs to detect behavioral regressions between a baseline and a new variant, investigate root cause with trace/span links, and take action (manual pause or automatic rollback) when thresholds are crossed. This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and initial implementation notes for the MVP dashboard, alerting rules, and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Console has a new 'Deployment Health' page listing active progressive deployments with per-variant KPIs: latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost per request, and quality regressions (per-eval score).
Users can select any two variants and see a side-by-side delta view with statistical significance hints and visualized histograms for latency, error classes, and embedding drift.
Each deployment row exposes a 'Drill into traces' action that filters distributed traces to the selected variant and highlights spans with elevated durations or error tags.
Anomaly scoring pipeline flags regressions with a confidence score and can trigger a customer-configurable auto-rollback policy (threshold + sustained window).
Alerting integrations: SNS/Webhook/Slack + per-deployment incident timeline. Alerts include example request IDs and links to sample prompts and responses for fast triage.
Performance: dashboard queries return within 2s for common queries (7-day window) and tracing samples do not increase baseline tracing cost by more than 15% (via sampling and index optimizations).
engineering_notes: Backend: extend metrics index to tag requests with 'deployment.variant' and 'traffic-mode' (canary/shadow/ab). Add pre-aggregated histograms for latency and token counts.

Traces: implement a trace-linker service that accepts a variant filter and returns sampled spans. Use existing trace storage but add variant index; keep default sample rate low and provide on-demand burst sampling for investigations.

Anomaly detection: use rolling-window baseline comparison with Bayesian uplift scoring (prototype in ENG-3445). Produce a 0-1 confidence score and expose contributing dimensions (tokens, prompt templates, model temperature).
Auto-rollback: implement webhook-based rollback hook in Serving API that accepts signed rollback requests; provide dry-run mode in Console and require an owner whitelist for auto-enabled policies.
Cost/Perf trade-offs: prefer approximate histograms (DDSketch) for memory efficiency; limit high-cardinality drilldowns to sampled datasets to avoid query explosion.
qa_plan: Create synthetic workloads to simulate 1) latency regressions, 2) increased hallucination metric (via eval harness), 3) token cost spikes. Verify dashboard flags and scoring matches ground truth.

End-to-end: create a canary deployment, inject synthetic errors for the canary only, validate Slack/SNS alert, validate that auto-rollback triggers when policy thresholds are met, and confirm serving reverts to baseline variant.
Security: verify rollback webhook only accepts requests signed by Console service account; verify audit log entry is created for every rollback action.

2025-03-01 Priya Singh (Design): Reviewed designs — recommended adding a ‘sample requests’ pane that surfaces raw prompts/responses and user metadata for quick triage. Added Figma comments with mockups.
2025-03-03 Rohit Malhotra (SRE): Raised concern about tracing sample rate increasing cost; proposed on-demand burst sampling and sample-weighted metrics to maintain SLOs.

2025-03-05 Arjun Patel: Spike complete — prototype for anomaly scoring demonstrates stable signals on historical A/B datasets (links in attachments). Need to finalize auto-rollback safety fences (owner whitelist, cooldown).
